name: Gateway 4 · Focus-15-style: 'no time'
summary: Go from Focus-10 and 12-style states into a deep, timeless open awareness, then look at one pleasant memory as an observer. Monroe called Focus 15 a state of 'no time'; the 1983 Army assessment linked it to travel into the past. A 7 Hz beat on Wahbeh et al.'s 133/140 Hz carriers is added; levels and order are our design. At the end you estimate how long the timeless part lasted; this is a rough self-check, not a blind measure, because the step list and the timer show the planned durations. Optional blinded helmet arm: 4 Hz, then 7 Hz in-phase sine, untested.
setting: Quiet room, dim (not dark) light, reclined or lying down, closed-back stereo headphones (needed for binaural mode; on speakers switch to isochronic mode). Not right after a heavy meal; empty your bladder and silence your phone. Best when you are rested. Never while driving.
cautions: Stop at once (count back and open your eyes, or move a finger) on dizziness, panic, headache or ringing ears. Do not use these sessions if you have epilepsy or photosensitivity, are in a psychiatric crisis or have a hearing problem, unless a doctor agrees. Keep the volume low: WHO advises an average of 80 dB(A) or less and device volume of 60 % or less. No driving, machinery or exams for at least 30 minutes afterwards: theta and delta beats did worse than beta beats on vigilance (Lane et al. 1998) and lowered recall against a noise control (Garcia-Argibay et al. 2019). Sound only; the app never uses flicker. This is an untested composite and not The Monroe Institute's program: no recordings, scripts or affirmation of theirs are used. Memory work can bring up distressing material (an MIAS brochure warns that repressed material can surface): choose a neutral or pleasant memory, and open your eyes and stop if you get upset. The helmet arm is experimental and runs only blinded (real or sham, revealed after your ratings): the god-helmet.com Shakti safety page advises against combining the helmet with binaural-beat devices in real time.

steps.title: Check-in and volume
steps.instructions:
Put on the headphones the right way round and lie back.

You hear soft pink noise, like distant surf, drifting slowly from side to side. Keep the volume you set at calibration, or turn it down until the sound is quiet and comfortable: the tones that follow are about 15 dB louder than this noise. Stay at or below 60 % device volume.

Try not to watch the step timer during the session. Rate how you feel right now.

steps.title: Short preparation
steps.instructions:
Close your eyes and go through the preparation at your own pace:

1. **Set-aside box:** turn each worry or task into a simple symbol, put it in a strong container and close the lid.
2. **Breathing:** slow breaths, filling the body region by region from the chest down to the feet; hold only if it is comfortable.
3. **Humming:** one long, steady tone on each out-breath; feel it in your head and chest.

The sound changes when it is time to move on.

steps.title: Focus-10-style: count 1 to 10
steps.instructions: Count from 1 to 10 and settle into the body-asleep, mind-awake balance.

steps.title: Focus-12-style: count 11 and 12
steps.instructions: Count eleven, twelve, and let your awareness widen.

steps.title: Count 13 to 15
steps.instructions:
Count thirteen, fourteen, fifteen, and let the sense of time thin out. No counting of minutes; just now.

*Sound: a 7 Hz beat (133 Hz left, 140 Hz right) joins; the beta layers become quieter (our design).*

steps.title: Timeless open awareness
steps.instructions: Rest as plain awareness. When thoughts of "how long" come up, let them go.

steps.title: Look at a memory
steps.instructions:
Choose one neutral or pleasant memory. Look at it as if from a quiet balcony: details, light, sounds, feelings, without judging. Leave it as it was.

Avoid painful memories. If you get upset, open your eyes and stop.

steps.title: Count back 15 to 12
steps.instructions: Count down from fifteen to twelve and pause there.

steps.title: Count back 12 to 10
steps.instructions: Count down from twelve to ten and pause there.

steps.title: Count back from 10 to 1
steps.instructions: Count slowly from 10 down to 1 and feel more awake with each number. Move your fingers and toes, stretch and open your eyes. Take back what you still want from the box.

steps.title: Estimate the time
steps.instructions: Before you look at any clock or at the timer, estimate how many minutes the timeless part and the memory part lasted together.

items.label: Timeless part plus memory part, in minutes (your estimate)

steps.title: Journal
steps.instructions: Now write down what you experienced, including how time felt.

steps.title: Session report
steps.instructions: Fill in the session report while the session is fresh.

steps.title: How you feel now
steps.instructions: Sit up slowly. Rate how you feel now, the same way as at the start.
